DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 66 s. 2022 JUL 22 2022 FORMER ACTING MAYOR RONALDO F. FRANCO Pamplona, Camarines Sur Dear Former Acting Mayor Franco: This pertains to your letter dated 22 June 2022 asking the Department's clarification on whether you and vice-mayor Josefa Fabi who assumed the positions as acting mayor and acting vice-mayor, respectively, of Pamplona, Camarines Sur, following the dismissal of elected mayor Gemino Imperial in 2019 relative to OMB-L-A-16-0551 , are entitled to full compensation due to the positions of Mayor and Vice-Mayor for two (2) years or from the time you started discharging the duties and functions of said positions. Per your letter and pertinent documents submitted to the Department, hereunder are the antecedent facts: In OMB-L-A-16-0551 , the Office of the Ombudsman dismissed elected Mayor Gemino Imperial; Accordingly, you, as the elected Vice-Mayor, assumed as acting mayor by succession; By virtue of a Designation issued by the DILG Secretary, 1st-ranking Sangguniang Bayan Member Josefa Fabi was designated as acting vice- mayor; From the time you and SB Member Fabi assumed as acting mayor and acting vice-mayor, respectively, which is more than two (2) years to date, your salary, RATA and other benefits are still based on your post as vice-mayor. Previously, the Department held the view, out of prudence, that dismissal from the service wherein the respondent local elective official availed or has pending remedies before the Office of the Ombudsman, the Court of Appeals or the Supreme Court assailing his dismissal order, is a temporary vacancy, not yet permanent, since the elected vice-mayor or next-in-rank's assumption to the Office of the Mayor or concerned office is still subject to the outcome of the aforesaid remedies availed of by the respondent elective official. However, the aforesaid view of the Department was corrected by the Supreme Court in Tallado vs. COMELEC, et al.l in this manner: 1 G.R. No. 246679, September 10, 2019. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"xxx inasmuch as Section 46 of the LGC textually applied to succession where the local chief executive was 'temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office,' the provision was certainly not the proper basis for the COMELEC to characterize as temporary the vacancy in the office of the Governor ensuring from the petitioner's dismissal. As earlier explained. the vacancy was not temporarv because the petitioner was fully divested of his title to the office of the Governor in both instances of his dismissal. Under Section 44 of the LGC, a permanent vacancy arises whenever an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, or refuses to assume office, or fails to qualify, or dies, or is removed from office, or voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office. In contrast, Section 46 of the LGC enumerates as resulting in a temporary vacancy in the office the local chief executive leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. Although Section 46 of the LGC specifically states that the causes of temporary vacancy are not limited to such circumstances, what is evident is that the enumeration therein share something in common, which is that there is a definite term to be re-assumed. However, the petitioner's dismissals. even if still not final were akin to the instances enumerated in Section 56 of the LGC because the loss of his title to the office denied to him the expectancy to re- assume his term Lastly, Section 44 of the LGC includes removal from office as one of the instances triggering a permanent vacancy. Such permanent vacancy was precisely the outcome that the OMB directed in its decisions. Consequently, when the petitioner was ousted in the period from November 8, 2016 to December 30, 2016, in the first instance of dismissal, and in the period from March 14, 2018 to September 26, 2018, in the second instance of dismissal, the permanent vacancy in the office of the Governor ensued." (Emphasis Supplied) This was reiterated in the SC Resolution dated March 2, 2021 in the same Tallado case, which resolved the motions for reconsideration filed by the private respondents and the Commission on Elections (COMELEC), thus: "In Our September 10, 2019 Decision, this Court ruled that the dismissal orders of the OMB against petitioner serves as permanent removal from office and was not merely temporary. From his dismissal until the Court of Appeals' modification of his penalty to suspension, petitioner neither had title nor powers to wield as governor of Camarines Norte. As evidence of this lack of title by petitioner, Camarines Vice Governor Jonah Pedro G. Pimentel was sworn as Governor, and not as Acting Governor. The nomenclature used here by the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) is important because it recognizes that the vacancy is not temporary but a permanent one. To rule otherwise would result in the absurd situation where a public office is occupied by two persons when basic in the law on public officers is that in single constituency positions, like the Office of the Provincial Governor, only one person can occupy a public office at a given time. The fact that the DILG has now clarified its position that it should have applied Section 46 of the Local Government Code, rather than Sec. 44, is irrelevant. As stated earlier, it is not the position of the DILG to characterize the nature of the dismissal of public officers being merely the implementor of the law.' Taking into account the Tallado case, the Department's issued DILG Opinion No. 130 s. 2021 Page 2 of 3

Applying the foregoing to your case and that of SB Member Josefa Fabi which are akin to the case of Tallado, we are of the view that you are both entitled to the remuneration and benefits accorded to the offices of the mayor and vice-mayor during those times that you assumed said positions in view of the dismissal of elected Mayor Gemino Imperial. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have provided the necessary guidance and clarification on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Undersec tary for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/kbm/clP Copy Furnished• ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA, CESO 111 Regional Director, DILG Region V Legazpi City VICE-MAYOR JOSEFA FABI Pamplona, Camarines Sur Page 3 of 3
